headline_cluster.headline: Afghan poppy cultivation more than quadruples despite Taliban ban; farmers say crops no longer feed families

claims.claim_he_or_en: Afghan poppy cultivation more than quadruples despite Taliban ban
claims.verified_figure: UNODC Afghanistan Opium Survey 2026: cultivation rose from ~10,200 ha (2025) to 43,300 ha (2026), +33,100 ha (+325%), i.e. x4.2
claims.note: 43,300/10,200 = 4.24, so 'more than quadruples' is correct for cultivation area. The 95% range is wide (32,000-61,000 ha), but the point estimate supports the headline.

claims.verified_figure: 43,300 ha (range 32,000-61,000) in the UNODC 2026 survey's provincial table; summaries round it to 'more than 43,000'
claims.note: Exact match with the survey's rounded national total. The article leaves out the wide uncertainty interval, which is normal for news copy.

claims.claim_he_or_en: In years gone by, Afghanistan's fields produced about 80% of the world's opium.
claims.verified_figure: UN News on the 2026 survey: before the ban Afghanistan supplied around 80% of global illicit opium
claims.note: Matches UNODC/UN News framing. The 2026 survey PDF itself does not repeat the 80% figure; it appears in UN News's report on the survey and in earlier UNODC reporting.

claims.claim_he_or_en: Sales this year generated an estimated $525 million, the highest figure since 2018 apart from 2022, when the ban sent prices soaring.
claims.verified_figure: USD 525 million total income of first-level traders in 2026 (vs USD 134 million in 2025); 'Apart from 2022, which was an anomaly ... the highest since 2018'
claims.note: Figure and ranking match the survey text almost verbatim. Small nuance: UNODC measures first-level trader income, not farmgate sales, and calls it comparable to the 2018-2021 average and well below 2017 and 2022 peaks.

claims.claim_he_or_en: Cultivation is still only about a quarter of the 177,000 hectares planted in 2021, the year before the ban.
claims.verified_figure: 177,000 ha in 2021 (survey table); 43,300/177,000 = 24.5%. 2022 (the ban year, planted before it took effect) was 233,000 ha
claims.note: The 2021 figure and the 'about a quarter' arithmetic are correct. UNODC's own 'pre-ban' benchmark is the 2022 crop (~232,000-233,000 ha), against which 2026 is under a fifth. Choosing 2021 is still a valid, clearly labelled comparison.

claims.claim_he_or_en: The Taliban rejected the findings, saying actual cultivation was about half the UN estimate and that eradication efforts continued.
claims.verified_figure: Annex 3 of the UNODC survey prints the response of the de facto Interior Ministry's counter-narcotics deputy ministry: its own estimate is 24,000 ha (55% of 43,300) and about 23,000 ha were eradicated. Spokesman Abdul Mateen Qani told Pajhwok that about 26,000 ha were identified (60%) and that the remaining area fell to almost zero after eradication.
claims.note: The rejection is correctly attributed and presented as a dispute, not as a UNODC figure. The 24,000 ha counter-estimate is about 55% of UNODC's figure, so 'about half' holds. Qani's press figure of 26,000 ha (60%) and his 'almost zero after eradication' line are vaguer versions of the same dispute.

claims.claim_he_or_en: UN agencies warned this month that 10 of Afghanistan's 34 provinces have critical levels of child malnutrition, a number that could reach 14 in 2027.
claims.verified_figure: The IPC acute malnutrition analysis (released 15 Oct 2026, cited by UNICEF and Action Against Hunger): provinces at critical levels rose from 7 (2025) to 10 (2026), projected 14 in 2027. Afghanistan has 34 provinces.
claims.note: The figures and timing ('this month') match. Strictly, the source is the IPC multi-partner analysis, released by UNICEF together with an NGO (Action Against Hunger). WFP's August 2026 figure of 12 provinces is a different count and does not contradict this.
